title: ML-MT126-MtLoopEndToEndProof

scope.summary:
GOAL: LIVE end-to-end proof of the FULL productized MT loop — the WP-017 packet-level acceptance criterion 'Full MT loop proven end-to-end' made executable. One integration proof drives: dispatch a REAL (small) hsk.microtask_contract@1 contract -> worker spawned with role+contract injected into an isolated session worktree -> worker implements and emits hsk.mt_signal@1 READY_FOR_VALIDATION as its structured exit -> MT-123 run advances -> orchestrator notified with ZERO polling (proven, not asserted) -> MT-124 validation handoff fires. Plus the three negative paths: BLOCKED signal, malformed signal, worker crash mid-run. This MT authors proof code + fixtures ONLY; any product defect it exposes is fixed in the owning MT (typed blocker + handback, never a silent patch here).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New integration test src/backend/handshake_core/tests/test_mt_loop_e2e.rs + fixture MT contract JSON + a machine-readable run report under the test tree; no product-source edits.

DETAILED SPEC — POSITIVE PATH (P-01):
1. Fixture contract: a real hsk.microtask_contract@1 JSON (fixture in the test tree, structurally template-conformant: wp_id, mt_id, lifecycle, scope.summary/allowed_paths/forbidden_paths/acceptance_criteria/proof_targets) whose objective is trivially implementable (e.g. create one file with fixed content inside the workspace and run one echo-style proof command).
2. Dispatch via MT-122: parse -> compose (role + objective + boundaries + hsk.mt_signal@1 output format + proof-target expectations) -> spawn through SwarmCoordinator. Worker lane: the cheapest live lane available per MT-027/MT-046 transport availability on the host; when no live CLI lane is available the harness's scripted/local worker lane executes the same transport contract (structured exit through the same parse path) — record WHICH lane ran; a scripted-lane run is a DISCLOSED degraded proof, not a silent substitute, and the live-lane run remains required for packet closure.
3. Workspace isolation: worker cwd = session worktree from ensure_session_worktree_allocation (workspace_safety.rs:370 — `git worktree add --detach` under session_worktrees/<session_id> or HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_ROOT), in MT-141 branch mode; assert the implemented file exists INSIDE the worktree and NOT in the main tree. VM binding: when a microVM adapter is available, exercise WorktreeVmRegistry::ensure_worktree_vm on the worktree (optional path); when unavailable, record the typed skip reason (adapter-unavailable) — never fake the VM leg.
4. Signal: worker's structured exit is hsk.mt_signal@1 READY_FOR_VALIDATION with evidence[] from its proof command and changed_paths; parsed by the MT-121 parser via the transport binding.
5. Advance + notify: assert mt_runs row walks DISPATCHED -> ... -> SIGNALED{READY_FOR_VALIDATION} -> VALIDATION_HANDOFF; assert the orchestrator notification (MT-105) was DELIVERED (recording sink) and the MT-124 handoff receipt exists.
6. ZERO-POLLING PROOF: over the dispatch->handoff window, scan the mechanical records (session/FR event stream, process ledger, notification log) and assert ZERO periodic status-query entries: no repeated state-read of the same run from the orchestrator side, no timer-driven poll events; the ONLY run-state reads permitted are event-triggered ones. Implement as: capture all bus/ledger entries in the window, classify with an explicit allowlist (dispatch, claim, transition, signal, notification, handoff, closure, test-harness assertions), fail on any status-query classification or unclassified read-loop pattern (>=2 identical reads of run state without an intervening event).
7. Cleanup: cleanup_session_worktree (workspace_safety.rs:418) on every exit path; assert no leftover worktree dir and `git worktree list` contains no stale entry.

NEGATIVE PATHS:
- N-01 BLOCKED: fixture worker emits BLOCKED with typed blocker {kind: MANAGED_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, detail}; assert run lands BLOCKED{blocker}, NO validation handoff fired, blocker visible via list_runs (the MT-125 data source).
- N-02 MALFORMED SIGNAL: worker exits with non-schema output; assert SignalParseFailure typed error recorded WITH bounded raw excerpt, run lands FAILED{SignalParseFailure}, no handoff, nothing silent.
- N-03 WORKER CRASH MID-RUN: kill the worker process after claim but before signal; assert the supervisor terminal report (or lease expiry as the fallback mechanism — record which fired) lands the run FAILED{WorkerCrashed | LeaseExpired}, event emitted, worktree still cleaned up.

RUN REPORT: the proof writes a machine-readable report (test tree, e.g. tests/mt_loop_e2e/last_run_report.json): { scenario_id, lane_used, live_or_scripted, vm_leg: exercised|skipped{reason}, states_walked, polling_scan: {entries_scanned, status_queries_found}, verdict } per scenario — the honest record a validator and the packet closure can cite.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the landed MT-121..125 surfaces + MT-027/046 transport bindings + MT-141 worktree-branch mode + MT-161 FR kinds in the product worktree; bind exact symbol names then author the test.
2. Author fixture contract + trivial workspace objective.
3. Implement P-01 with lane selection + disclosure, worktree/VM assertions, zero-polling scan, cleanup guards (Drop-based so panics still clean up).
4. Implement N-01, N-02, N-03.
5. Emit the run report atomically (temp+rename).
6. Run everything against a live backend with managed PG per the crate's integration conventions; record measured outcomes; typed blocker (NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF) instead of green language if the managed resource is unavailable.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml ([[test]] registration only if required by crate convention)
forbidden_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/** (proof-only MT: product defects hand back to the owning MT via typed blocker, never patched here)
app/src/** (legacy React; GUI surface exception exists only on the board MT MT-125)
.GOV/** (the product READS MT contracts; it never writes .GOV — the fixture contract lives in the test tree)
acceptance_criteria: P-01 passes live: fixture contract dispatched, worker spawned with role+contract injected, work performed INSIDE the session worktree (asserted in-worktree and absent from the main tree), READY_FOR_VALIDATION structured exit parsed, run walked to VALIDATION_HANDOFF, orchestrator notification delivered, handoff receipt recorded.

Zero-polling PROVEN mechanically: the dispatch->handoff window scan reports 0 status-query entries and 0 unclassified read-loop patterns over the captured bus/ledger records — a number in the run report, not a claim.

Worktree leg uses ensure_session_worktree_allocation in MT-141 branch mode; VM leg exercised via WorktreeVmRegistry::ensure_worktree_vm when an adapter is available, else recorded as typed skip (adapter-unavailable) — never faked.
N-01: BLOCKED signal lands BLOCKED{typed blocker}, no handoff fires, blocker queryable via list_runs.
N-02: malformed exit lands FAILED{SignalParseFailure} with bounded raw excerpt recorded; no handoff; no silent path.
N-03: worker killed mid-run lands FAILED{WorkerCrashed or LeaseExpired — mechanism recorded}; event emitted; worktree cleaned up.
All scenarios clean up session worktrees on success AND failure paths (Drop guards); `git worktree list` shows no stale entries after the suite.
Machine-readable run report written atomically with lane disclosure (live vs scripted), VM-leg status, states walked, polling-scan numbers, and per-scenario verdicts.

If any leg cannot run against its real resource, the result is a typed blocker (NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF / adapter-unavailable) in the report — PASS language is never written for an unexercised leg.
proof_targets: python -c "import json;r=json.load(open('src/backend/handshake_core/tests/mt_loop_e2e/last_run_report.json'));assert r['P-01']['polling_scan']['status_queries_found']==0;assert all(s['verdict'] in ('PASS','TYPED_BLOCKER') for s in r.values());print('e2e report OK')"
git -C . worktree list | grep -c session_worktrees | grep -q '^0'
expected_tests: P-01 full-loop live scenario incl. in-worktree work assertion + notification delivery + handoff receipt
zero-polling window scan with classification allowlist
N-01 BLOCKED / N-02 malformed / N-03 crash scenarios
implementation_notes: This MT is the packet's honest gate for the operator's core productization claim; it deliberately mirrors the operator's live repo-gov loop (orchestrator -> coder -> validator handoff) at product level. The run report is the citeable artifact — treat it like MT-045's perf_manifest.json (atomic write, honest statuses, typed blockers instead of green language).

Scripted-lane fallback exists so the loop mechanics are provable on a host without live CLI credentials, but it is ALWAYS disclosed in the report (live_or_scripted) and packet closure requires at least one live-lane P-01 run — do not let the fallback become the only evidence.

The zero-polling scan allowlist must be explicit and enumerable in the test source so a validator can audit what counts as legitimate reads; err on the side of failing the scan and widening the allowlist consciously.

Crash-path note: whether supervisor terminal report or lease expiry fires first is timing-dependent; the assertion accepts either but REQUIRES the mechanism to be recorded — both are mechanical, neither is polling.

Windows host: session worktree paths and git worktree cleanup have Windows-specific failure modes (long paths, locked files while the child is dying); N-03 must wait for child-process exit before cleanup assertion, mirroring workspace_safety.rs's own discipline.
Fixture contract ids use a reserved test namespace (e.g. wp_id WP-TEST-E2E, mt_id MT-900 range) so no collision with real governance ids is possible in reports/ledgers.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless integration proof; the operator surface (board) is verified in MT-125. The run report is the trace projection.

target_entries: MT dispatch loop: what happens from dispatch to validation handoff (mechanical signals, no polling)
Reading the MT loop run report; interpreting BLOCKED / parse-failure / crash outcomes

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.obligation: last_run_report.json exposes per-scenario lane, VM-leg, states walked, polling numbers, and verdicts to any no-context model.
The proof consumes and asserts the FR/bus/ledger trace itself (the zero-polling scan IS a trace audit).
Run outcomes are visible on the MT-125 board (runs created by the proof appear as rows); UserManual entry ships same-change.

risk_if_missed: The productized MT loop ships assembled-but-never-proven: polling could silently persist, negative paths could dead-end runs invisibly, and the WP's central acceptance criterion (full loop end-to-end, zero polling) would rest on unverified claims.

risks: RISK-1: The scripted-lane fallback quietly becomes the only evidence and the 'live loop proven' claim is actually a self-test of the harness.
RISK-2: The zero-polling assertion is vacuous — the scan classifies everything as allowed or scans an empty window, proving nothing.
RISK-3: The proof patches product code to make itself pass (scope bleed), hiding defects from the owning MTs' lineage.
RISK-4: Worktree/VM legs are mocked or skipped without disclosure, so isolation is asserted but never exercised.
RISK-5: Crash-path flakiness (timing between supervisor report and lease expiry) turns N-03 into a retried-until-green test that masks real supervision gaps.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): run report discloses live_or_scripted per scenario; acceptance requires live-lane P-01 for packet closure; scripted-only is a typed degraded verdict.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): scan must report entries_scanned > 0 and the allowlist is enumerated in test source; a canary sub-test injects one synthetic status-query record and asserts the scan FAILS on it (scanner self-proof).
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): src/** is a forbidden path for this MT; defects hand back via typed blocker naming the owning MT; proof target diff-scope check belongs to the validator's mechanical track.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): in-worktree/not-in-main-tree file assertions + typed VM-leg skip reasons; no mock worktree.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): N-03 accepts either mechanical mechanism but records which fired; no retry loop around the scenario — a flake is a finding, not a rerun.

research_provenance.source: WP-017 stub acceptance criteria ('Full MT loop proven end-to-end ... zero polling') + operator rules (polling forbidden; no green language without live proof; typed blockers) + verified product code: workspace_safety.rs ensure_session_worktree_allocation:370 / cleanup_session_worktree:418 / HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_ROOT:357, worktree_vm_registry.rs ensure_worktree_vm:94 / snapshot:117 / restore:129, coordinator.rs spawn/lease/reaper, events.rs sinks + MT-045 honest-manifest precedent (atomic report, typed non-PASS statuses).
corrections: Zero-polling is proven by a self-proving scanner (canary injection) over captured mechanical records, not by absence-of-code review alone.
VM binding is an optional exercised-or-typed-skip leg because microVM adapters are host-dependent (worktree_vm_registry fake-adapter seam precedent); the worktree leg is mandatory.
